title: Flow steps: make first+last a frame-owned TEMPLATE, so a FlowDef only declares the middle
description:
Fabio, 2026-08-16, on seeing foley gain a middle step: every Flow has the SAME first stage (supply inputs) and the SAME last stage (generate + result); only the in-between varies. That shape should be a template the frame owns once, not something re-expressed per flow - 'instead of repetition in code'.

WHERE IT STANDS TODAY: the frame is ALREADY half-way there and that is worth knowing before touching it. `_buildInputsSlide` and `_buildRunSlide` are frame-owned and no FlowDef declares them; `steps: []` really does mean 'no middle steps'; and the ticker derives itself ('Inputs' + middles + 'Generate'). So the repetition Fabio is reacting to is NOT the slides - it is what each FlowDef still has to restate around them: `inputSchema.media` labels, `controls` vs step `fields` (two vocabularies for the same widgets, landing in different places in the payload), and the run-slide `uiComponent` escape hatch.

THIS IS MPI-531's ACCEPTANCE CLAUSE IN DISGUISE: 'the FlowDef is fully expressible as a third-party manifest'. A manifest cannot carry JS, so anything the frame does not own by default is a thing a third-party Flow cannot have. Design the default template with that test, not for the three built-ins.

OPEN QUESTION for the next session to settle WITH Fabio: should `controls` (run slide) and step `fields` collapse into ONE declaration surface? They already share a renderer (`_buildField`) and, since 2026-08-16, the same payload law - a field id `Input_*` becomes an injectionParam, anything else goes top-level. Two names for one concept is the repetition he is pointing at.

Sibling of MPI-531 (authoring shape) under the MPI-560 Flow track.
